intended_object: The homeomorphism X ≃ f(X) given by a topological embedding f : X → Y, with f(X) carrying the subspace topology. Inferred from the docstring "Homeomorphism given an embedding" and the type X ≃ₜ Set.range f.
explanation: The body first builds the bijection X ≃ range f, x ↦ ⟨f x, _⟩, with Equiv.ofInjective, using injectivity of f. It then upgrades it to a homeomorphism with toHomeomorphOfIsInducing. For that it shows the corestriction is inducing: since f = Subtype.val ∘ corestriction and Subtype.val is inducing, IsInducing.of_comp_iff applies, and f is inducing because it is an embedding. An inducing bijection is exactly a homeomorphism, so this is the standard construction. The only hypotheses are the topologies on X and Y and that f is an embedding, which is exactly what the statement needs, so it is at its natural generality. A grep of Mathlib/Topology found no other declaration of the same object.
